label: prop:categorical-mass-markov
title: Categorical mass as Markov trace
html:
The categorical mass descends to the Iwahori–Hecke algebra. Single-level categorical mass evaluates to the absolute value of the Markov trace.

Statement

Proposition. Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) form a quantum observable universe with Frobenius–Hopf object A = H_n(R, q) over a commutative ring R. Let \varrho \colon \mathbf{1} \to A form a closed cycle representing the knot \mathcal{K} with braid representative \beta_\mathcal{K} \in B_n. The single-level categorical mass satisfies

  \mathfrak{m}_{q,\mathcal{K}}\big|_{\text{single level}}
  \;=\; \Bigl|\!\int_A\! \rho(\beta_\mathcal{K})\Bigr|,

where \int_A : A \to R is the Jones–Markov trace, functioning as the Frobenius integral on A.

Modulus isolates the bar-even shadow

The absolute value operation isolates the bar-even (\cosh, real-q) component of the Markov trace. This provides the mass or binding channel. The discarded bar-odd (\sinh, root-of-unity-q) component provides the imaginary part of the complex fibre observable \mathfrak{V}, where \mathfrak{V} = \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{bind}} + i\,\mathfrak{Q}_\beta. This imaginary part equals the \beta-decay Q-value, \mathfrak{Q}_\beta = \mathrm{Im}\,\mathfrak{V}.

Mass and \mathfrak{Q}_\beta construct the two parities of a single object (conj:binding-qbeta-complex-volume). We take the modulus only when the mass magnitude alone is required. Any computation tying binding to decay must retain the bar-odd shadow. This requires the root-of-unity evaluation, rather than collapsing to the modulus.

The parameter q_0 is not complex. At the observable level, \mathrm{Im}(q_0) = 0. The imaginary part forms the fibre-level shadow, which constitutes a separate real observable.
